questions.prompt: Why must an earthworm's skin stay moist for it to breathe effectively?

questions.prompt: Why is excreting nitrogen mainly as uric acid useful to many birds and reptiles?

choices.text: It dissolves more readily than urea in water
It allows waste removal with relatively little water
It uses less energy than excreting ammonia directly
It eliminates nitrogen without losing any carbon

questions.hint: Compare a concentrated paste with a large volume of dilute liquid.
questions.explanation: Uric acid is poorly soluble and can be eliminated in a concentrated form. Producing it costs energy but helps conserve water.

questions.prompt: In a cold-water bird's leg, warm arterial blood flows beside cooler venous blood. What is the main benefit?

choices.text: Arterial and venous blood mix before reaching the heart
The blood's freezing point rises as it enters the foot
Heat returns toward the body before reaching the foot
Heat is carried more efficiently from the core to the foot

questions.hint: Follow the heat separately from the direction of blood flow.
questions.explanation: Countercurrent exchange transfers heat from outgoing arterial blood to returning venous blood, reducing heat lost through the extremity.

questions.prompt: Why does opposite-direction flow of water and blood improve oxygen uptake in fish gills?

choices.text: It makes oxygen diffusion independent of concentration
It equalizes oxygen levels at the midpoint of the gill
It replaces diffusion with active pumping of oxygen
It maintains an oxygen gradient along the exchange surface

questions.hint: Compare conditions along the entire gill, not just at its entrance.
questions.explanation: Countercurrent flow keeps water relatively richer in oxygen than the adjacent blood over much of the gill, sustaining diffusion.

questions.prompt: A bony fish moves from fresh water into seawater more concentrated than its body fluids. Which osmotic tendency reverses?

choices.text: Net water flow ceases despite the concentration difference
Net water gain becomes net water loss
Net water loss becomes net water gain
Net salt gain becomes net water gain

questions.hint: Track water movement across a membrane before considering the fish's compensating behavior.
questions.explanation: Water tends toward the more concentrated solution. The fish gains water in fresh water but tends to lose it in seawater, requiring different regulation.

questions.prompt: A hypothetical animal doubles every linear dimension without changing shape. If oxygen demand follows volume, what happens to demand per unit of outer surface area?
questions.hint: Compare how area and volume scale, then take their ratio.
questions.explanation: Doubling length multiplies area by four and volume by eight. Demand per unit surface therefore doubles, helping explain the need for internal exchange surfaces in larger animals.

metadata.author: OpenAI
metadata.verificationNotes: Verified scaling independently: (2 cubed)/(2 squared)=2. Idealized constant shape and volume-proportional demand are explicit; not a claim about actual whole-animal metabolic scaling.
